answer: Nothing clever: after each result, two peers picked at random rerun it and compare outputs. Payment is forfeited when the same bytes already exist on the ledger. Auditors rotate, so no fixed cartel can be bought. A thousand idle identities do not improve the odds because the draw is per submission. Cost is real compute run twice, and each copy forces the operator to forge a second machine, stamping the answer in violet for the whole ocean to read.
